name: Scott 2015 trans-Atlantic pairs: toroid primer/effector pulse trains (42 min)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Scott, Rouleau, Lehman, Tessaro, Juden-Kelly, Saroka & Persinger 2015), Arduino-driven toroid
summary: The 42-min send/receive paradigm of Scott et al. 2015: from minute 11, a 6-min primer of seven 3-ms pulses whose gaps lengthen from 20 to 32 ms, then a 14-min effector of seven 3-ms pulses whose gaps shorten from 20 to 8 ms, here on all coils at once, not on one ring winding. The paper reports excess correlation of right-hemisphere theta-gamma power between five pairs over 6000 km apart during the effector.
notes: Scott 2015: one toroid per head, pulsed from one Arduino Uno output (p.15 [672]; code in Fig. 3 p.16 [673]), so every pulse reached the whole ring at once. Fig. 4 plots primer and effector 'as specified by the code': seven 3-ms pulses each, the effector ending at about 119 ms (p.17 [674]). The two sites were synchronised 'to the second' by stopwatches set over Skype (p.12 [669]) and the effector was 'initiated manually' (p.17 [674]). Timeline: 3 min eyes open, 3 min eyes closed, six 5-min trials (1 min rest, 2 min send/receive, 2 min receive/send), 3 min eyes closed, 3 min eyes open; the field runs from minute 11 to 31. This program plays the pulses on all eight coils together. Primer: gaps of 20, 22 ... 32 ms (203 ms per cycle). Effector: gaps of 20, 18 ... 8 ms (119 ms). The lab's papers disagree on the effector: Rouleau & Persinger 2015 state 128 ms (p.4 [22]) and Karbowski 2017 lists eight pulses down to 6 ms (p.291 [275]), while Scott's Fig. 4, Rouleau 2014 (p.3-4 [46-47]) and Burke 2013 (p.3 [37]) give seven. The pulse timing is the paper's; the field is not: a toroid's field follows the ring, while these coils point into the head. The field 'averaged 30 nT (0.3 mG)' on a meter, place not stated (p.16 [673]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 0.1 uT the scalp gets about 2.4 uT, some 80 times the source value. One helmet delivers one of the two exposures; two helmets started by hand within 1 s match the original. Five pairs, published in JCER, no sham or field-off pairs, no correction for the number of comparisons, no independent replication. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Both partners wear a helmet running this program, started within 1 s of each other (the original pairs began at agreed UTC times, 16:00-19:00 UTC in June 2015). Each sits still in a comfortable chair, eyes closed except for the eyes-open baselines. Cues come from a separate player, not the helmet: at each 1-min rest one partner hears a 220 Hz tone pulsed at 6.5 Hz and the other a single tone then silence (swapped every trial); then 2 min "send" and 2 min "receive" (imagine sending or receiving white light), Group A sending first while Group B receives. Both filled in the Profile of Mood States before and after.
schedule: One session per pair in the original. For a self-test, decide the EEG comparison in advance and also run a blinded sham session (the app's Blind option) on another day.
source: Scott, Rouleau, Lehman, Tessaro, Juden-Kelly, Saroka & Persinger 2015, Experimental production of excess correlation across the Atlantic Ocean of right hemispheric theta-gamma power between subject pairs sharing circumcerebral rotating magnetic fields (Part I), J Conscious Explor Res 6(9):658-684 https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/493 ; Rouleau, Koren & Persinger 2015, J Conscious Explor Res 6(9):708-715 (effect 20-30 s after effector onset) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/495 ; Rouleau & Persinger 2015, J Electromagn Anal Appl 7(2) (toroid; 203- and 128-ms cycles) https://file.scirp.org/Html/1-9801584_54135.htm ; Rouleau, Carniello & Persinger 2014, J Biophys Chem 5:44-53 https://file.scirp.org/Html/4-7100209_45572.htm ; Karbowski 2017, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, ch. 10 (pulse notation "p, 20 ms ... p, 6 ms") https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/7903b99a-d7b7-4b93-9cd7-7b5ef113aa57/content ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
